abstract: Relating tongue motion measured with dynamic MRI to the speech it produces could inform rehabilitation after glossectomy. Prior studies have translated cine or tagged MRI into log-mel spectrograms and used the two-dimensional Pearson correlation between predicted and recorded spectrograms (Corr2D) to quantify the acoustic information captured by each imaging modality. However, Corr2D has not been calibrated against MRI-free predictors that preserve basic acoustic structure. Our contribution is an evaluation framework for speech synthesis from cine MRI, tagged MRI and their combination; the synthesis network is held fixed. On identical leave-one-subject-out folds, we compare four trained input configurations with two MRI-free controls: a static mean-spectrum baseline and a time-aligned cohort template. Across 44 subjects (18 after glossectomy) producing two utterances, the cohort template, which never sees an MRI, reached a Corr2D of 0.745 and 0.664. The static baseline, which contains no timing, reached 87 to 89% of that score. No trained configuration outperformed the template on Corr2D, a cepstral distance or ESTOI; seven of the eight fell significantly short on Corr2D. For cine MRI this held across three positional encodings, an encoder temporal-attention module and a training objective matched to the metric. Cine and tagged MRI differed consistently within subjects, although the direction depended on the metric. Absolute Corr2D alone therefore does not show that a model recovers acoustics from the MRI. The two controls are a reusable method: any study can compute them from its own training recordings, so a model's margin over them measures what its images contribute.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对动态 MRI 到语音合成中 Corr2D 虚高且缺乏校准的问题，论文固定同一主干比较 4 种 MRI 输入与两种无 MRI 对照，发现队列模板以 Corr2D 0.745 和 0.664 持平或超越所有模型，而静态均谱已占模板分数 87–89% ，代价是结论仅限双短语单中心数据与特定渲染。
originalTitle: Evaluating Cine and Tagged MRI-to-Speech Synthesis with Complementary Metrics and MRI-Free Controls
readerTitle: 无 MRI 对照揭示磁共振到语音合成评价的虚高
